svg.aria-label: Three sufficient routes, with a rank-two construction

a.xlink:title: For a finite admissible quadratic presentation P, the full degree-one action obeys A_S(P) = D M_S(α_P) = −D M_S(Z_P). The singular term A₀ = ½Dδ(Σcνhνkν) is retained. Full first derivatives commute with M_S, including polyhedral boundary contributions.

P is the specified admissible finite quadratic actual zero on the same ordinary representative as its full-exact identity. S is any allowed original background of degree 0 ≤ p ≤ n−2; retain all original compact smooth tests and actual refinements. Full derivative compatibility gives M_S(α_P) = d′(β ∧ S) + d″(ζ ∧ S). Applying D kills both terms by nilpotence and anticommutation. No higher-degree arbitrary-current product is assumed.

P is the specified admissible finite quadratic actual zero, with exact a_j, ε_j → 0 and a single positive represented Q on one fixed ordinary neighborhood. The represented order estimate transfers to the all-background degree-one action for every allowed 0 ≤ p ≤ n−2; Q and the neighborhood do not vary with the test or later refinement. Each exact a_j has zero differentiated action. The fixed positive control bounds every remaining compact pairing by ε_j times a finite fixed mass; distributional continuity of D then gives zero. Approximating only Z_P retains the complete singular A₀ term.

On one ordinary representative chosen for P, α_P = d′β + d″ζ in the actual delta-form sheaf. This is a hypothesis available in proved special cases; its existence for every quadratic actual zero remains open. It does not require a continuous smooth-form double primitive.

Actual symmetric full-exact forms a_j approximate α_P in the represented order interval −ε_jQ ≤ [α_P]−[a_j] ≤ ε_jQ, with ε_j → 0 and one fixed positive represented Q. The all-background degree-one estimate is part of this certificate. The same ordinary domain, Q and approximants precede later backgrounds, tests and refinements.

For the specified closed carrier F, the unchanged carrier-CLN seminorm of P vanishes at every required enlarged compact stage. Only the permitted harmonic, pointwise-zero-product and ambient-cycle generators are used. Whether every actual PL-zero has the required absolute-cap certificates is open; zero action does not imply this stronger certificate.

Here P is a finite quadratic PL curvature polynomial and S is an allowed background carried by the specified unchanged closed F, in a legal degree. Zero seminorm holds at every enlarged compact stage required for the test, using finite decompositions on the same ordinary domain and only the permitted generator space. An absolute-cap certificate directly kills its relative capped background. Returning from all such caps to an uncapped S uses the separate KC9 detector: q = n−(p+b) > 0 and 1 ≤ c ≤ max(q mod 2, q−2 floor(p/2)). That proposition gives no positive-rank cap route when q = 0 or this upper bound is zero. Permitted carrier relations act by zero. Apply the uniform carrier-only CLN estimate to each remainder and take the seminorm infimum. This proves a sufficient annihilation criterion; it does not identify the actual analytic kernel or all seminorm polars.

The action A_S(P) is zero on all original compact smooth complementary tests under any one incoming sufficient route and that route’s displayed hypotheses. Exactness and fixed-control approximation allow every legal S. The direct carrier theorem allows the S carried by its specified F. This node does not assert that every actual relation already has such a certificate.

For an actual quadratic zero in a fixed finite continuous closed-cell PL/PS presentation with joint residue rank s_f(x) ≤ 2, the source construction returns a full strain covector to the whole actual moment image. It constructs both full first-order exactness and fixed-Q approximants on an ordinary neighborhood, in arbitrary ambient dimension.

The fixed relation is an actual quadratic zero in the finite continuous closed-cell PL/PS class, and its entire original scalar tuple f satisfies s_f(x) ≤ 2. Use the constructed ordinary neighborhood and finite actual original-unit refinement; all lower strata and later deficient-rank refinements remain included. The normal-surface construction returns a continuous finite-PS covector whose full strain is Z_P on the whole actual moment image. Since A₀ = ½Dδu is already full-exact, α_P = A₀−Z_P has an actual first-order exact expression.

Retain the same actual zero, full finite closed-cell source data and joint bound s_f(x) ≤ 2. Fix 1 < κ < 2 and one ordinary truncation before later backgrounds and tests. Regularize the returned continuous covector and use the finitely many coefficient facets, |ℓ_H|^κ and a fixed strictly convex term to construct one positive Q = D[q]. The source-side all-background estimate is O(δ^((2−κ)/2)); setting a_j = A₀−e_δj yields the required full-exact approximation.

Impose the stronger intrinsic bound s_K(x) ≤ 2, so the union tuple of any two finite presentations has joint residue rank at most two. For a sheaf morphism, this bound holds at every point of the ordinary open; local finite presentations and the actual quotient sheaf are retained. Two presentations of one actual quadratic curvature differ by an actual zero. Apply rank-two exactness to their union tuple, so their transgression classes agree. The singular A₀ is exact, and ordinary sheaf gluing gives τ₂ with D̄τ₂ = id. Separate rank bounds on the two tuples alone would not justify this argument.

If the entire residue dimension satisfies s_K(x) ≤ 2, the quadratic transgression class depends only on the actual quadratic curvature. The canonical map τ₂ satisfies D̄τ₂ = id. These classes glue on ordinary opens satisfying the bound, including analytic surfaces. Separately low-rank presentations are insufficient unless their union tuple also meets the bound.
These incoming deductions are alternatives, with their own stated hypotheses.
